# ARCH-19: New behaviour is opt-in, and lands as the last and smallest commits of a PR

- A change to what a vehicle does is off by default - behind a parameter, an option bit or a feature define - so no one's aircraft behaves differently after an update they did not ask for. The exceptions are a fix for an actual bug, and a change a maintainer agrees should be on by default; the PR says which.
- Within a PR the structure comes first: refactoring and plumbing in commits that change no behaviour, shown where possible to leave the compiler output unchanged (`Tools/scripts/size_compare_branches.py`, or `--consistent-builds` builds hashed per commit), then the behaviour change last, as a small surgical set of commits a reviewer can read on its own. A refactor mixed into a functional change hides what actually changed and makes both harder to review. On the RP2350 branch ([#32995](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/32995)) MatekH743 copter stayed binary-identical through the first 45 commits, and the six that changed STM32 output came after them, each saying so.

Confirmed 2026-10-16. Part of the root playbook, under [Architectural Principles](../claude/CLAUDE.md#architectural-principles). [All architectural rules](../README.md#architectural-rules)
